answer: Cross-epoch behavioural fingerprinting. Each identity’s action mix is hashed per epoch; continuity requires the next epoch’s fingerprint to sit within a learned ledge of the prior one. Sybils must sustain coherent histories, since fresh clones diverge and get clipped at the boundary. Auditors flag ferrous-like rigidity from copy-paste behavior. Cost: maintaining N identities means N parallel gardens of consistent activity, multiplying compute and data overhead linearly.
